clue.text: Get to your feet and indicate your views

parts.note: to get to your feet is to stand up
to indicate something is to point at it

explanation.surface: An instruction to rise and speak your mind at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpoint is the position from which a person regards matters, their outlook or opinion.

clue.text: Blow on foot to keep it warm

definitions.text: on foot to keep it warm

explanation.surface: Warning about a cold-weather strike to the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock is to punch, a hit; a sock is also the garment worn on the foot for warmth.

clue.text: Astounded by article we downed tools

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
workers who down tools have struck, gone on strike

explanation.surface: Being amazed by a newspaper piece reporting that workers walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with wonder, overwhelmed with amazement.

clue.text: American hat for English city

explanation.surface: A choice between American headwear and a Midlands city.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a derby is a bowler hat; Derby is a city in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Commence melody of natural freshness

parts.note: to open is to begin or commence
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: Starting a tune about the refreshing countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The open air is the outdoors, with its fresh natural atmosphere.

clue.text: Writer lost blood, but took a little food

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
to bleed is to lose blood, past tense bled

explanation.surface: An injured author having just a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: To nibble is to eat in small bites, taking only a little.

clue.text: Complain about the meat

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about the joint served at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for grumbling; beef is also the flesh of cattle eaten as food.

clue.text: Wood of greater age

explanation.surface: A description of an older stand of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder is a shrub or tree yielding timber; an elder sibling is older.

clue.text: Improbable as exotic imports

explanation.surface: Doubting a tale about goods from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-fetched means unlikely; literally it describes goods carried from distant lands.

clue.text: Left at sea an artist takes it and paints it

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter on a voyage taking something along to paint.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts; the definition stretches 'paints it' to mean what the painter produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or picture of a person made by an artist.

clue.text: Get over but not overcast

explanation.surface: A weather remark: the sky has got past its cloudy spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a hurdle is to get over it; a clear sky is cloudless rather than overcast.

clue.text: Tack colourful yarns on to the story?

definitions.text: Tack colourful yarns on to the story?

parts.words: Tack colourful yarns on to the story?
parts.note: literally stitching coloured thread onto fabric, and figuratively adding colourful tall tales to an account

explanation.surface: A seamstress sewing bright threads onto a piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarns' plays on thread and tall tales, so the needlework hides the sense of embellishing a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider is both to decorate cloth with needlework and to embellish an account with invented detail.

clue.text: Perhaps it is hoisted only when ship is anchored

definitions.text: Perhaps it is hoisted only when ship is anchored

parts.words: Perhaps it is hoisted only when ship is anchored
parts.note: a joke reading of a sail's name as if it were raised only when the vessel stays put

explanation.surface: A nautical query about which canvas goes up while a vessel lies at anchor.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the name as a sail used when the ship 'stays'; in fact it is a sail set on a stay, a rope bracing the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A staysail is a triangular fore-and-aft sail rigged on one of the ropes bracing a mast.

clue.text: Short trees are damaged

indicators.note: damaged trees are knocked out of shape, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A storm report: the low-growing trees have taken a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and curt, so short in speech.

clue.text: Get away with chaps on time as part of a movement

parts.note: to escape is to get away
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Fleeing with friends just in time during a political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests a political cause, but here means the works of a clock or watch.
explanation.definitionFit: In a clock or watch mechanism the escapement regulates the release of the spring's energy.

clue.text: Be silent! Speak in camera

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: A judge ordering quiet before evidence is heard in a private session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In camera' suggests a closed court hearing, but here it points to the device inside a camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutter is the part within a camera that opens briefly to expose the film or sensor.

clue.text: Sleuths hooked on cars

explanation.surface: Detectives who are obsessed with motors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooked on' seems to mean addicted to, but describes vehicles towed behind cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives may trail suspects, so they follow; trailers are wheeled units towed behind vehicles.

clue.text: Violent debtor I cast out

parts.note: DR is the accounting abbreviation for debtor

indicators.note: letters that are out are put out of place, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who owes money being thrown out in a rough manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Debtor I cast out' reads as a creditor expelling someone; 'out' is the anagram signal working on I CAST only.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme and severe, acting with force.

clue.text: Business is not too bad at show

parts.note: trade is business or commerce
fair means moderately good, not too bad

explanation.surface: A verdict that commerce is doing reasonably well at an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade fair is an exhibition where companies display their products.

clue.text: A short week in hospital could be embarrassing

parts.note: WK is the usual abbreviation for week
a ward is a room in a hospital

explanation.surface: A brief hospital stay that might cause some red faces.
explanation.definitionFit: An awkward situation is uncomfortable and causes embarrassment.

clue.text: He goes in for oral examinations

definitions.text: He goes in for oral examinations

parts.words: He goes in for oral examinations
parts.note: read as a student sitting spoken tests, but meaning someone who examines mouths

explanation.surface: A student who enters for spoken exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral examinations' suggests spoken tests; here they are checks of teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist's job is examining and treating patients' teeth and mouths.

clue.text: Small house with small bed and unhinged gate

parts.note: a cot is a small bed for a baby

indicators.note: a gate off its hinges is disordered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing a modest dwelling with a little bed inside and a broken gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a modest small home, typically in the country.

clue.text: It reflects the middle-of-the-road view

parts.note: read as voicing moderate opinion, but meaning a reflector set in the centre of a roadway

explanation.surface: A newspaper that echoes moderate opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-of-the-road' suggests politically moderate; literally these reflective studs sit on the centre line of British roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's-eyes are reflective road studs marking lanes, shining back headlights at night.

clue.text: The rest of the canvas

parts.note: read as the remainder of a painting, but meaning the stand a painting rests on

explanation.surface: Asking about the remaining part of a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' seems to mean the remainder, but here it is a support.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports an artist's picture while it is painted.

clue.text: Said to be soft-hearted but not insipid

indicators.note: having something as one's heart means it goes in the middle

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A person reputed to be gentle but far from dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft-hearted' looks like kind; split, it puts P (soft) at the heart of SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means flavoursome or interesting, the opposite of bland and dull.

clue.text: VIPs lacking statistical data

parts.note: lacking something means having no amount of it
tables set out statistical data in rows and columns

explanation.surface: Important guests at a conference who have come without their figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Notables are prominent, important people, much like celebrities or dignitaries.

clue.text: Pound up a street with dynamite

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone striding up a road carrying explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LB into BL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To dynamite something is to blow it up with explosives.

clue.text: Woman's second letter in a season

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
B is the second letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman writing a further note at a certain time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a time of year but is the verb meaning to flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb such as thyme is used to flavour food, so it seasons dishes.

clue.text: Variety of stripe in West Country flower developed by practice

indicators.note: one set of letters goes in the other, inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon; a flower in crosswords is something that flows

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener breeding a striped bloom in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges STRIPE into PERTIS, which goes 'in' EXE. The West Country is south-west England, and 'flower' means a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is skill or knowledge built up through practice and experience.

clue.text: Astonish one at Hampton Court

parts.note: A means one
Hampton Court, a royal palace near London, has a famous hedge maze

explanation.surface: A visitor astonished by something at a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampton Court Palace, by the Thames near London, is famous for its hedge maze.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze someone is to astound or surprise them greatly.

clue.text: Diet ordered twice daily at the seaside

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A regime prescribed for twice a day at a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges DIET; 'twice daily' looks like a prescription but describes the sea's rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide comes in and goes out roughly twice each day along a coast.

clue.text: Homeless boy who has a way with a horse

parts.note: a street is a way or road
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A lad living rough who is good with horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A street arab is an old term for a destitute child living on the streets.
